1168.1: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Chaupade Dutuke, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Of all the months, blessed is the month in which the spring that never ends (the Lord) has come (into the mind). Blossom, O my mind, keeping that Gobind (the Lord of the universe) (within you) for ever and ever. O simple (mind), let go of the awareness bound to Haumai (ego). O mind, subdue Haumai and reflect, and take up and keep the virtue that is the best of all virtues. Let (good) deeds be the tree, (remembrance of) the Lord its branches, dharma its flower and the knowledge (of God) its fruit; let the attaining (of the Lord) be its leaves, and the end of the mind's pride its dense shade. (Then) the eyes (behold the Lord's) creative power, the ears (hold his) Bani, and in the mouth the only speech is the True Name; the wealth of honour has been made full, and the attention is fixed in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise). The months and the seasons keep coming (and going); practise such deeds and see. O Nanak, those who remain merged (in the Lord) through the Guru stay green and never wither. ॥4॥
1168.2: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The delightful season of spring has come; in it, those dyed in your love dwell on you with eager joy. To whom (but you) should I make offerings in worship? At whose feet should I fall? O Sovereign Lord, I call myself the slave of your slaves. O Life of the world, (to meet you) no other way is found. Your being is one, (yet your) forms are many. To whom (but you) should I make offerings in worship? To whom should I offer incense? No one has found your limit; where could (anyone) find it? O Sovereign Lord, I call myself the slave of your slaves. (For me) the sixty years of the calendar's cycle and all the places of pilgrimage are your True Name, O Supreme God. Your state, O Unmanifest Lord, cannot be known; without knowing it, one should utter (your) Name. What can poor Nanak say? All the world praises you, the One. Nanak's head is at the feet of those people. I am a sacrifice to all your Names, as many as there are. ॥4॥
The sixty years (sathi sambat): the sixty-year cycle of the Hindu calendar, each year with its own name.
1168.3: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (If one has) a cooking square of gold, pitchers of gold, lines of silver (drawn round it), a great array (of purity), water of the Ganga, fire kindled as for a sacrifice, (and) eats a meal of boiled rice mixed with milk, O mind, (all this) never comes into the account as long as (the mind) is not soaked in the True Name. (If one) has the eighteen (Puranas) written out beside him, recites the four Vedas by heart, bathes (at the pilgrim places) on holy days, gives alms as laid down for each varna, (and) keeps fasts and observances day and night; (if some) become qazis, mullas, sheikhs, yogis, jangams, wearers of saffron robes, (or) someone a householder bound up in rituals, without understanding (the Lord), all are bound and led away. On the head of every being is written the work (set by the Lord's command): by (each one's) deeds will (each) be judged. The foolish and ignorant issue their own commands; O Nanak, the treasures of praise belong to the True One. ॥4॥
Fire as for a sacrifice (karante ki aag): fire made by rubbing two sticks of wood together, held pure for the yajna. Jangams are Shaiva mendicants who go about ringing bells.
1169.1: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (One) may cast off his clothes and go naked as a Digambar; what Yoga does he practise by wearing matted hair? The mind does not become pure (by raising the breath) to the Tenth Gate; wandering and wandering, (such) a fool comes (into birth) again and again. Meditate on the One, O foolish mind, (and) you will cross over in an instant. (Some) expound the Simritis and the Shastras; those who sound the nad (the yogis) and those of the Vedas (the pandits) read the Puranas; (but their) gaze is hypocrisy, (and) in their minds they practise deceit; the all-pervading Lord is not near them. Even if someone is so self-disciplined (that) he performs special rites and worship, (if) greed is within (him) and the mind is in the poison of Maya (the world's illusion and lure), how can such ones find the Immaculate Lord? What can come of what the created being does? (He alone walks) whom the Lord himself makes walk. If (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, then he dispels doubt; if (one) understands the Hukam (God's will and command), then one finds the True One. One whose inner self is filthy may roam the places of pilgrimage and the lands of the world, (yet his bonds do not break). O Nanak, (when) one finds the company of the True Guru, then the world-ocean's bonds are snapped. ॥5॥
Digambar (sky-clad): a Jain ascetic who goes naked. The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
1169.2: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) in all the worlds is the attachment of your Maya. I see no other; you are all. You are the Master of the gods and the Naths, the God of gods. The Lord's Name is obtained by serving the Guru's feet. O my beautiful, deep and profound Beloved, Through the Guru (one) sings the praises of the Name of Ram; you are beyond the farthest, the Sustainer of all. Without the Saadh (the Guru), the Lord's company is not obtained. Without the Guru, the body stays soiled with filth. Without the Lord's Name, (no one) becomes pure; one who praises (the Lord) through the Guru's Shabad (the Word) is true. O Protector, the one whom you protect you unite (him) with the True Guru and take (him) into your care. (He) casts off the poison of Haumai and possessiveness; O Sovereign Lord, all (his) sorrows are destroyed. Exalted is the state and the measure of one in whose body are the Lord's virtues; by the Guru's teaching the diamond of the Name of Ram shines forth (in him); leaving the love of another, (his) love is fixed on the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). O Lord, unite your servant Nanak with the Guru, with the Guru. ॥4॥
1169.3: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). My friend, my companion, listen with love: my Husband is the fount of delight; she with whom he is (is the blessed bride). He is unseen and cannot be seen; tell me, how (can he be seen)? The Guru has shown me the Sovereign Lord right beside (me). Come together, my friend, my companion; (singing) the Lord's praises is what becomes (us). The brides of the Husband who play with the Lord God, seeking (him) through the Guru, have their minds won over. The forsaken manmukh (self-willed) brides do not know this secret: that he, the Beloved of all, delights in every heart. The Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) recognises the eternal Divine Lord at her side; the Guru has made the Name firm (in her), and she repeats it. Without the Guru there is no devotion and no love; without the Guru, the Sant (saint), (the Lord) does not grant his company; without the Guru, the blind one weeps (caught) in worldly entanglements; through the Guru the mind becomes pure, (as) the Shabad washes away its filth. (She) whose mind the Guru has subdued, bringing about the union, enjoys day and night the union of devotion. In the assembly of the Guru, the Sant, sorrow and disease are wiped out; O servant Nanak, (she gains) the Lord as Husband, and union in Sahaj. ॥4॥
1170.1: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). He himself fashions and makes his creation; the True One, ruling his own rule, himself settles (every account). By the Guru's sublime teaching (he is seen) with (us), at (our) side; the Lord's Name is the elixir, the (true) wealth (gained) in Sahaj. O mind, utter (the Name of) Ram; do not ever forget (him). The Lord is beyond the farthest, beyond reach, beyond the senses, beyond all weighing; through the Guru he himself lets (himself), the Unweighable, be weighed (in the heart). (O Lord,) your Gursikhs serve the Guru's feet; by the Guru's service they cross over, leaving behind mine and yours. Slanderous and greedy men, hard of mind, who have not loved the Guru's service, are thieves of thieves. The Guru, when pleased, bestows devotion and love; when the Guru is pleased, a place in the Lord's mansion is obtained. Cast off slander and keep awake in the Lord's devotion; the Lord's devotion is beautiful; by (his) grace (it comes to be one's) lot. The Guru unites (one) in his union and gives (the) gift (of the Name); (to him) the Gursikhs are dear, day and night. The fruit, the Naam, is obtained (when) the Guru, pleased, gives it; says Nanak, rare are those who obtain it. ॥4॥
1170.2: Raag Basant, an Iktuka, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). If it pleases the Master, the servant serves (him); he dies (to himself) while yet alive, and saves all his generations. (O Lord,) I will not give up your devotion; what does it matter if anyone laughs? (Your) True Name dwells in my heart. As a mortal stays absorbed in attachment to Maya, so the Sant stays dwelling on the Name of Ram. (O Lord,) show mercy to me, foolish and ignorant, (that) I may stay lying at your refuge. Says Nanak, the works of the world bear no fruit; by the Guru's grace, some (rare one) obtains the Name, the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life). ॥4॥
1170.3: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Brahmin, worship and win over (the Lord): let that be your saligram; let good deeds be your rosary of tulsi. Build a raft by repeating the Name of Ram, (and pray:) have mercy, O Merciful Lord. Why do you water barren, salty ground and waste your life? The wall of unbaked clay will fall; why do you coat it with lime plaster? Let (the service of) your hands be the Persian wheel; string the pots on its chain, and yoke the mind to it; draw up the Amrit, fill the beds (of the field); then you will belong to the Gardener. Make lust and anger both into hoes, brother, and dig the earth (of the body). As you dig, so will you find peace; the work you have done is not wiped out. (O Lord,) if you are merciful, the heron becomes a fair swan. Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, humbly prays: have mercy, O Merciful Lord. ॥4॥

Basant Hindol: the shabad is sung in Basant blended with the raag Hindol. The saligram: a round, veined stone from the river Gandaki, worshipped as a form of Vishnu; a rosary of tulsi (holy basil) is worn by his worshippers.
The swan stands for the pure in mind, the heron for one who looks white but lies in wait for fish (the hypocrite).
1171.1: Raag Basant Hindol, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). All the goods given from the in-laws' house (by the Husband) are to be shared, yet in the parents' home (the world) I, the bride, kept them apart. I myself am without the art of living; I blame no one (else); I did not know how to keep (what was given). O my Master, I myself have strayed, lost in doubt. I sing only the letters written (in my lot); I know no other way to shape (my life). If (brides) embroider (virtues) and wear the bodice, then know them for (true) women. If they guard their house and taste no evil, they become dear to the Husband. (O pandit,) if you are learned, a wise pandit, (know that) the two letters (of the Name) are the boat. Nanak humbly prays: the One (Name) alone carries (me) across, if I stay merged in the True One. ॥3॥
1171.2: Raag Basant Hindol, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The king (the mind) is a child, the city (the body) is unbaked, (and his) love is for the wicked (passions). Two mothers and two fathers are spoken of (for him); O pandit, reflect (on this). O revered pandit, give (me) counsel: by what means may I find the Lord of my life? Fire is within, (yet) the vegetation is in bloom; the ocean is held within a lump (of clay); the moon and the sun, both, are within the one house: such knowledge (you) have not gained. One who puts an end to the one mother (Maya) is known as one who dwells on Ram; his marks are known (thus): he gathers the wealth of forgiveness. (The mind) dwells with those (senses) alone that do not hear what is told them and are never satisfied with what they eat. Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, humbly prays: (the mind) is one moment a tola, the next a masha. ॥4॥
Tola and masha: weights for gold; a tola is twelve mashas.
1171.3: Raag Basant Hindol, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Guru, the giver of peace, is the true banker; he unites (one) with the Lord and takes away the hunger (for Maya). In his grace he makes devotion to the Lord firm (in one), (and himself) sings the Lord's praises every day. O mind, do not go astray: remember the Lord. Without the Guru there is no liberation in the three worlds; through the Guru the Name of the Lord is obtained. Without devotion the True Guru is not found; without good fortune there is no devotion to the Lord. Without good fortune the Sat Sangat (the company of the true) is not found; by (his) grace the Name of the Lord, Har, is obtained. Hidden in every heart, (the Lord) creates and watches over (all); through the Guru he is manifest to the Sants. Those who repeat Har Har are drenched in the Lord's love; the Lord's water, the Amrit Name, (is in their) minds. Those who, through the Guru, are given the glory of the throne, (the Lord) has made eminent. Meeting the paaras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold: the Guru), they have become paaras; O Nanak, (they) have become companions of the Lord and the Guru. ॥4॥
1172.1: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Dutuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O Lord,) in all the months and seasons (you are) the spring that lasts for ever, by which every being and creature is kept green. What can I say, a mere worm? Your beginning and your end no one has found. (O Lord,) those who serve you, the Master, obtain the supreme bliss, O Divine Light of the soul. If there is (the Lord's) grace, then (one) serves (him); by the Guru's grace (one) dies while yet alive; every day (one) utters the True Name; in this way the mortal crosses the (world-ocean) so hard to cross. The Creator has made poison and Amrit (both); he has set two fruits on the tree of the world. The Creator himself does and has (all) done; as it pleases him, (so) he feeds each one. O Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace he himself gives the Amrit Name, and checks (in his mind) the craving for Maya's poison; (the Lord) himself carries out his own will. ॥4॥
1172.2: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those dyed in the True One, in the Lord's Name, are in bliss. O God, merciful to the meek, have mercy (on me). Apart from him I have no one else; as it pleases (him), so he keeps (me). The Guru, Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), is pleasing to my mind; I cannot live without beholding (him); when the Guru unites (me) in his union, I meet (him) in Sahaj. This greedy mind is lured by greed; forgetting Ram, it repents afterwards. Those dyed in the Guru's service, separated, (the Lord) unites (with himself); to those with great good fortune (written) on their foreheads, (he) has given the Lord's Name. This body, this frame, is (made) of air and water; in (this) body is the disease of Haumai, its pain severe. (For one who) through the Guru has sung (the Lord's) praises, the Name of Ram is the medicine; in his grace the Guru has rid (him) of the disease. In the body are four rivers of fire, all four; (people) burn in thirst for the world, burn in pride. The fortunate ones whom the Guru has protected (he) has carried across; O servant Nanak, (they) hold the Lord's Amrit in their hearts. ॥4॥
The four rivers of fire: cruelty, attachment, greed and anger.
1172.3: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Whoever serves the Lord is the Lord's own; (he has) the true Sahaj, (and) sorrow never comes (to him). The manmukhs are dead (within), (for) the Lord is not in their minds; dying and dying they are born, and again they die. Those people live in whose minds is the Lord; they keep the True One in mind (and) are merged in the True One. Those who do not serve the Lord are far from the Lord; they wander through foreign lands, (and) throw dust on their heads. The Lord himself has drawn (his) servants (to himself); they have peace for ever, (and) not a trace of greed. (When the Lord) casts his glance of grace, pride departs; (one) receives honour in the True Court. (He) sees the dear Lord ever present; through the Guru's Shabad (he sees him) filling all. (The Lord) cherishes every being and creature; (the one who) by the Guru's grace keeps him ever in mind goes from the True door to (his own) home with honour; O Nanak, through the Naam (one) obtains greatness. ॥4॥
1173.1: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (True) worship is within, done with the mind; (such a worshipper) sees the One alone and no other. In the love of another, people have suffered great pain; the True Guru has shown me the One. My God, the spring that lasts for ever, is in full bloom; singing the praises of Gobind, this mind has blossomed. Ask the Guru, and reflect; then love for the True God takes hold. If, giving up self, you abide in the spirit of a servant, then the Life of the world comes to dwell in (your) mind. (One who) does (the Lord's) devotion sees (him) ever present; my God is ever filling all. Rare is one who knows the secret of this devotion: my God, the Divine Light of the soul, is all. (The Lord) himself unites (one) with the True Guru; he himself attaches (one's) consciousness to the Life of the world. (Their) mind and body become green, naturally, in Sahaj; O Nanak, (they) remain attuned to the Naam. ॥4॥
1173.2: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Lord, the Lover of devotion, comes to dwell in the mind, by the Guru's grace, naturally, in Sahaj. (When one) does devotion, losing self from within, then alone is there union with the True One. The devotees ever look beautiful at the door of the Lord God, (held) in love for the Guru, in love and affection for the True One. The one who does devotion becomes pure; through the Guru's Shabad he loses Haumai from within. The dear Lord himself comes to dwell in (his) mind; (he) stays ever merged in peace, in comfort, in Sahaj. For those dyed in the True One it is the spring that lasts for ever; (their) mind and body are green, dwelling on the praises of Govind. Without the Name the world is dry; it burns again and again in the fire of craving. (One who) does only what pleases the dear Lord (and) fixes his consciousness on (the Lord's) will has peace in his body for ever; (he) serves his God naturally, in Sahaj; O Nanak, the Naam comes to dwell in (his) mind. ॥4॥
1173.3: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (One who) burns away attachment to Maya through the Shabad has his mind and body turned green through love for the True Guru. At the Lord's door (his) tree has borne fruit, through the True Bani, through love of the Name. O mind, (you will) turn green, naturally, in Sahaj; through love for the True Guru the fruit of truth grows (on you). (The Lord) himself is near, he himself is far; through the Guru's Shabad (one) sees him ever present. Dense is the shade, the vegetation is in bloom: the Gurmukh blossoms, naturally, in Sahaj. Every day, day and night, they sing Kirtan (songs of God's praise); the True Guru has removed filth and doubt from within (them). Beholding (the Lord's) expanse of creation, (one) is lost in wonder; through the Guru the gift of the Name is obtained. The Creator himself enjoys all tastes and pleasures; whatever he does, that alone surely comes to pass. (He is) the great Giver, without a trace of greed; O Nanak, (he) is met by living the Shabad. ॥4॥
1174.1: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (One who) by perfect fortune does the work of truth (and) remembers the One does not come into the womb again. Fruitful is the birth of (such a one) who has come into this world, (who is) merged in the True Name, in Sahaj. Through the Guru, do (this) work with your love attuned: serve the Lord's Name, losing self from within. That servant's word is true, (and) through the Guru's Shabad it pervades the world. Through the four ages (his) true glory spreads; the servant dyed in the Name becomes known (to all). Some stay attuned to the True Shabad; those people are true, (held) in love of the True One. They meditate on the True One, beholding (him) ever present, (and are) the dust of the lotus feet of the Sants. The Creator is One; there is no other; through the Guru's Shabad union (with him) comes about. Whoever has served the True One has found the delight (of the Name); O Nanak, (he) is merged in the Naam in Sahaj. ॥4॥
1174.2: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Lord's servants worship him, beholding him ever present, (and are) the dust of the lotus feet of the Sants. They stay ever attuned to the Lord; the perfect True Guru has given (them) this understanding. Rare is the one who becomes the slave of (the Lord's) slaves; he alone attains the highest state. Serve the One alone; there is no other (like him), serving whom there is peace for ever. He neither dies nor comes and goes; O mother, why should I serve any other but him? True are those people who have recognised the True One; killing self, they have merged in the Naam in Sahaj. Through the Guru the Naam is obtained; (then) the mind becomes pure, (and in it dwells) that pure True One. Know the Lord who brought forth wisdom (in you); through the True Shabad recognise the One God. When one tastes the Lord's delight, then comes awareness; O Nanak, those dyed in the Name (find) that True One. ॥4॥
1174.3: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those dyed in the Name save their generations (too); (in them is) the True Bani, the love of the Name. Why did the strayed manmukhs come (into the world)? Straying from the Name, (they) have wasted their life. One who dies while yet alive, by so dying makes his death a fine one; through the Guru's Shabad he enshrines the True One in his heart. The Gurmukh's food is truth, his body is pure; his mind is pure, (and he is) ever a deep (ocean) of virtues. He is not born, does not die, does not come and go; by the Guru's grace he merges in the True One. Serve the True One; (whoever does so) recognises the True One, (and) through the Guru's Shabad bears the mark (of approval) at the Lord's door. At the True Door he has true glory; he finds a dwelling in his own (true) home. He himself never errs; he is true, wholly true; all others go astray in duality and lose their honour. Serve the True One through the True Bani; O Nanak, (the awareness of those who serve) stays merged through the Name in the True One. ॥4॥
1175.1: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without (the Lord's) grace, all (the world) is led astray by doubt; in attachment to Maya it suffers great pain. The blind manmukh finds no place of rest; a worm of filth, he is absorbed in filth. One who obeys the Hukam is accepted; through the Guru's Shabad, through the Name, (he bears) the mark (of approval). Those in whose lot (the Lord) wrote it from the very first are dyed in the True One; the Lord's Name is ever pleasing to their minds. Through the True Guru's Bani there is peace for ever; it merges (one's) light in the Light (of the Lord). The One Name alone carries the world across; by the Guru's grace (comes) love for the Name. Without the Name no one has attained liberation; from the perfect Guru (alone) the Name comes into one's keeping. That one understands (this) whom (the Lord) himself makes understand; through service of the True Guru (the Lord) makes the Name firm (in him). Those who have known the One are accepted; O Nanak, dyed in the Name, (they bear) the mark (of approval) at (the Lord's) door. ॥4॥
1175.2: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (On whom the Lord) shows grace, (him) he brings to meet the True Guru, (and) himself, of himself, comes to dwell in (his) mind. (His) understanding becomes steady, (his) mind ever composed; he sings the praises of the Lord, the deep (ocean) of virtues. Those who stray from the Name eat the poison (of Maya) and die; their life is wasted; they come and go again and again. They put on many religious garbs, (yet) no peace comes to the mind; in great pride (one) loses one's honour. Fortunate are those who have recognised the Shabad; they have brought (the mind) that ran outside back home. Within the home is the treasure (the Name) of the inaccessible, infinite (Lord); (those who), by the Guru's teaching, search (for it) through reflection on the Shabad have found the Name, the nine treasures, within the home itself; ever dyed in (his) love, they stay merged in the True One. (The Lord) himself does (all); nothing can be done (by anyone of himself); when it pleases him, he himself unites (one with himself). No one is near him, and no one is far; O Nanak, through the Name (he is seen) pervading everywhere. ॥4॥
The nine treasures (nav nidh): in Puranic lore, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; here, every kind of wealth.
1175.3: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Remembering the Lord with love through the Guru's Shabad, (one) stays satisfied with the delight of the Name of Ram. The sins of millions upon millions (of lives) are burnt away; they die while yet alive and stay merged in the Lord's Name. (To whom to give) the Lord's gift the dear Lord himself knows; through the Guru's Shabad this mind has blossomed, (and) it utters the Name of the Lord, the giver of virtues. Wandering in saffron robes there is no liberation; by much self-restraint no one finds peace. Through the Guru's teaching the Naam is obtained; one of great good fortune alone finds the Lord. In Kalyug glory comes through the Name of Ram; (it) is obtained from the perfect Guru. Those dyed in the Name find peace for ever; without the Name (one) burns in Haumai. By great good fortune (one) reflects on the Lord's Name; through the Name of Ram all (his) pain departs. He who dwells in the heart is the expanse (of the world) outside; O Nanak, the Creator knows all. ॥4॥
1176.1: Raag Basant, Iktuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O Lord, I am) a worm, a creature made by you; if you give it, then I may repeat the primal Mantra (your Name). O my mother, may I speak (his) virtues and reflect on them, (and,) repeating the Lord's Name, fall at the Lord's feet. By the Guru's grace (people) are drawn to the taste of the Name; (O brother,) why do you waste your life in enmity and strife? (On whom) the Guru showed grace, (his) pride was ended; naturally, in Sahaj, he obtained the Lord's Name. Noble and high is the work of the Shabad; Nanak utters the True Name. ॥4॥
1176.2: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The vegetation has blossomed; spring has come; in the True Guru's company this mind has blossomed. O foolish mind, meditate on the True One; then, O my mind, you will find peace. With this mind in bloom, bliss has come; the Amrit fruit, the Name of Gobind, has been found. Everyone speaks and declares (that God is) One, only One; (but only) when one understands the Hukam does one know the One. Says Nanak, no one (then) speaks in Haumai; speaking and seeing, all comes from the Master. ॥4॥
1176.3: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O Lord,) all the ages are made by you; when the True Guru is met, understanding and wisdom come. O dear Lord, unite (me with yourself), you yourself, (that) through the Guru's Shabad (I may) stay merged in the True Name. (Those who have) spring in the mind are all green in the world; they bear fruit and blossom; through the Name of Ram there is peace. (For one who) reflects on the Guru's Shabad it is the spring that never ends; he keeps the Name of Ram enshrined in his heart. (When) spring is in the mind, body and mind turn green. O Nanak, this body is a tree; he obtains (on it) the fruit, the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
1176.4: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Spring is for those who sing the Lord's praises; by perfect fortune (alone) the Lord has (one) worship him. This mind is not touched by even a breath of spring; this mind is burnt in duality, in double-mindedness. This mind, bound in worldly affairs, does deeds (to match); robbed by Maya, it ever cries out in pain. This mind is released when the True Guru is met; then it does not come again under the blow of Jamkaal (death). This mind is set free; the Guru has freed it; O Nanak, (he) burns away attachment to Maya through the Shabad. ॥4॥
1176.5: Raag Basant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Spring has come; the vegetation is in bloom; these beings and creatures blossom, fixing their minds on the Lord. In this way this mind turns green: (when) one repeats day and night the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and through the Guru washes Haumai out. The True Guru proclaims the Shabad through the Bani; through love for the True Guru this world turns green. Fruit and flowers grow (only) when (the Lord) himself makes them grow; one clings to the Root (the Lord) when one finds the True Guru. (The Lord) himself is the spring; the whole world is (his) garden; O Nanak, (his) unique devotion comes by perfect fortune. ॥4॥
1177.1: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I am a sacrifice to the Guru's Bani, O brother; I give myself up to the Guru's Shabad. Ever I praise my Guru, O brother; I fix my mind on the Guru's feet. O my mind, fix your attention on the Name of Ram; obtaining the one fruit, the Lord's Name, your mind and body will turn green. Those whom the Guru protected were saved, O brother, (when he) gave them the Lord's delight, the Amrit, to drink. The pain of Haumai left (them) from within, O brother, and peace came to dwell in (their) minds. Those whom (the Lord) himself forgave from the very first, O brother, he has united (with himself) through the Shabad. By the dust of their (feet) one is set free, O brother, joining the union of the Sat Sangat. He himself has (all) done and himself does it, O brother, he who has made everyone green. O Nanak, peace ever dwells in mind and body, O brother, (for one whose) union (with the Lord) comes through the Shabad. ॥4॥
1177.2: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Iktuke, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. As the light of the sun's rays is spread (everywhere), so the all-pervading Lord is woven like warp and weft through every heart. The One Lord pervades all places; O my mother, through the Guru's Shabad (he) is met. Within every heart is that One Lord; when the Guru is met, the One becomes manifest. The One, only One, is pervading all; (yet) greedy Saakat men think (him) far away. The One, only One Lord, is at work in the world; O Nanak, what the One Lord does, that comes to pass. ॥4॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
1177.3: Raag Basant, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Night and day, the two, are sending out the call (of death); O mind, remember the Lord: at the end and always he saves. O my mind, ever remember the Lord, Har Har. (Those who remember him) have found God, breaking all sloth and pain; (so,) through the Guru's teaching, sing God's praises. The manmukhs die again and again in Haumai; the demon Death has struck them down, and they have gone to the city of Jam. (Those who) through the Guru are attuned to the Lord, Har Har Har, are rid of both pains, of birth and of death. The Lord has shown grace to his devotees; Guru Nanak was pleased, and Banwari (the Lord) was met. ॥4॥
Banwari (wearer of the garland of forest flowers, a name of Krishna): in Gurbani, a name of God.
1178.1: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Name of Ram is a chamber of jewels, hidden away in one (place) in the palace of the fortress (of the body); if the True Guru is met, it is searched out, and (one's) light, meeting the Light, merges in it. O Madho, bring me to meet the holy; beholding (them), all sins are destroyed, and (one) attains the pure, supreme state. The five thieves (lust and the rest) together break into the city (of the body) and steal the wealth of the Name of Ram; when, by the Guru's teaching, their tracks were followed, they were caught, and the wealth, the capital, was saved whole. (People) have grown weary of the ways of hypocrisy and doubt; within (their) hearts is Maya, Maya alone. (One who) has found the holy Being, the Lord of men (the Guru), has driven out the darkness of ignorance. (Whom) the Lord of the world, the God of the universe, the Master of creation, in his grace brings to meet the holy (Guru), O Nanak, peace comes within (his) mind; he ever sings the Lord's praises in his heart. ॥4॥
Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God.
1178.2: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). You are the great Being, the great Inaccessible, O Lord of the world; we are lowly worms of yours. O Lord, merciful to the meek, O God, show grace: it is the feet of the Guru, the True Guru, that we yearn for. O dear Gobind, in your grace unite (me) with the Sat Sangat. I am filled with the filth of the sins of birth after birth; O God, joining (me) to the Sangat, make (me) clean. (O Lord,) your servant, whether of high caste or low, who has repeated the Lord's Name, has turned from fallen to pure; the Lord has raised (him) above all the worlds; the Lord God has given (him) glory. Of high caste or low, whoever meditates on God has all his hopes fulfilled. Blessed are those servants of the Lord, great, great and perfect, who have enshrined the Lord in their hearts. We are lowly, dull as clods, exceedingly heavy (with sin); O Lord God, show grace and meet (us). Servant Nanak has found the Guru, the Lord being pleased; (the Guru) has made us, the fallen, pure. ॥4॥
1178.3: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My mind cannot live a moment (without the Name); it is ever given over to the delight of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as a child clings with relish to its mother's breast, and when the breast is drawn away, cries and wails. O dear Gobind, my mind and body are pierced by the Lord's Name. Great is my fortune: I have come upon the Guru, the True Guru, (and) within the city of the body found the Lord. Every breath of the Lord's servant, as many as there are, is pierced by longing for the Lord God, as the lotus has a very deep love for water, and without seeing the water it withers. The servant has repeated the spotless Name of Narhari; through the Guru's teaching the Lord (is seen) before him. The filth of Haumai of birth after birth has gone, (as he) bathed in the Lord's Amrit, the Lord's water. O Master, do not weigh our deeds; keep your own honour. O Lord, if it pleases you, hear (my) plea and prayer: servant Nanak has sought your refuge. ॥4॥
Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1179.1: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). From moment to moment the mind runs about, wandering and wandering; not for an instant does one find a dwelling at home. (When) the Guru has set on (its) head the goad of the Shabad, (the Shabad,) the remedy, (the mind) is brought back and settled in its home, its temple. O dear Gobind, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat, (where) one meditates on the Lord. (There) the disease of Haumai is gone, peace is found; in Sahaj one is absorbed in the Lord in samadhi. The home (of the body) is laden with jewels, rubies and many gems, (but) with the mind wandering, they cannot be found. As the Od (the well-digger) brings to light in an instant a well hidden (under the earth), so through the True Guru the thing (the Name) is found. Those who have not found such a True Guru, the holy one: cursed, cursed is the life of those men. The treasure of human birth was obtained as the fruit of merit, (but) it goes in exchange for a shell (kauddi). O Madhusudan, O Lord, O God, show grace; in your grace bring (me) to meet the Guru. Servant Nanak has attained Nirvana, the state beyond all desire; meeting the holy (Guru), one should sing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1179.2: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Coming and going, the pain of Maya, are (his lot); the manmukh's body is empty, utterly empty. (He) has not remembered the Name of Ram for a moment, an instant; Jam, Death, has seized (him) by the hair. O dear Gobind, rid (me) of the poison of Haumai and possessiveness. The Guru's Sat Sangat is dear to the Lord; joining the Sangat, (may I) enjoy the Lord's delight. (O Lord,) in your mercy unite (me) with the Sat Sangat of the holy, (that I may) fall at the refuge of the Saadh. We are sinking stones: O God, pull (us) out; you are merciful to the meek, the destroyer of pain. O Master, place the Lord's praise within (my) heart, (that,) joining the Sat Sangat, (my) understanding may be lit. Love for the Lord's Name has taken hold of us; we are a sacrifice to the Lord. O Lord God, fulfil the hopes of (your) servant; give (me) the Lord's Name, the Lord's light.
1179.3: Bliss has come to servant Nanak's mind and body: the Guru has given (him) the Mantra, the Lord's praise. ॥4॥
1180.1: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Dutuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I serve the Guru, bowing to him; today in my (home) are songs of joy, today in my (home) is great bliss: my anxiety has lifted, (for) I have met Gobind. Today it is spring in my home: I have sung your praises, O infinite God. Today Phaag has come to my (home); God's companions have come together and begun to play. I have made the service of the Sants my Holi; the deep crimson colour of the divine Lord('s love) has taken hold (of me). My mind and body have blossomed, beautiful beyond compare; they do not wither in shade or in sun; in every season they are green: meeting the divine Guru, it is the spring that lasts for ever. The Parjat tree has sprung up (within me), bearing flowers and fruit like jewels of every kind. Singing the Lord's praises, (I am) satisfied and fulfilled; servant Nanak meditates on the Lord, Har Har Har. ॥4॥
Phaag: Holi, the spring festival of the month of Phagun. The Parjat: the wish-fulfilling tree of Indra's heaven.
1180.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The shopkeeper keeps his shop for wealth and goods; the gambler's mind is on gambling; the addict lives by taking his drug: so the Lord's servant lives, meditating on the Lord. Each one is absorbed in his own love; to whatever God has attached (him), to that he is attached. When the clouds gather, the peacocks dance; seeing the moon, the night-lilies blossom; seeing her child, the mother is in bliss: so the Lord's servants live by repeating (the Name of) Gobind. The lion ever craves meat for food; seeing the battle, the warrior's heart is thrilled; the miser has a great love of wealth: (so) the Lord, Har Har, is the support of the Lord's servant. All loves are (held) in the one love (of the Lord); the peace above all peace is in the Lord's Name. This treasure is obtained only by him to whom, O Nanak, the Guru gives it as a gift. ॥4॥
1180.3: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Spring is for him on whom God is gracious; spring is for him on whom the Guru is merciful; there is joy in the (home) of him whose one work is (the One Lord); the spring that lasts for ever is for him in whose heart is the Name. Spring is counted to be in the home of him in whom is the Kirtan of the Lord, its melody. O mind, blossom in love of the Supreme Lord; one should practise wisdom by asking the Lord's servants. He alone is an ascetic who has the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy); ever in meditation is he who has the Guru's love. Those are without fear in whom (the Lord's) fear has settled; he is at peace whose doubt is gone; he is a recluse whose heart stays in its place; he alone is steadfast (who rests) in the True place. (One who) seeks the One alone, (whose) love is for the One, (in whose) mind is the longing to see (him) and to touch (his feet), (who) in Sahaj enjoys the colours of the Lord's love: servant Nanak is a sacrifice to that person. ॥4॥
1181.1: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you gave the soul, the breath of life and the body; placing (your) Light (within), you made the fool beautiful. All are beggars, O God; you are merciful; repeating the Naam, (they) are in bliss. O my Beloved, able to do all things, I receive everything from you. Repeating the Naam, one is saved; repeating the Naam, (one finds) the sublime peace of Sahaj; repeating the Naam, honour and glory come; repeating the Naam, no obstacle stands in the way. That for which this rare body (was given), that Word, O my God, give (me). May this (mind) find its rest in the Saadh Sangat, (that) I may ever repeat your Name, O God, in my heart. There is none but you; all is your play; (all) merge in you. As it pleases you, so save (me); O Nanak, (there is) peace (when) the perfect Guru is met. ॥4॥
1181.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The beloved God, the Sovereign, is with me; O mother, (he is the one) seeing whom I live, by whose remembrance no pain comes: in (your) mercy, unite me with him. O my Beloved, support of my breath of life and my mind, this soul and breath of life, all of it, is your wealth. He whom godlike men and gods seek, whose secret the silent sages and Shesh Nag (the serpent of a thousand tongues) do not find, whose state and extent cannot be told, is pervading every heart, every heart. He whose devotees are filled with bliss, whose devotees know no decay, whose devotees have no fear, whose devotees ever have victory: what praise of yours can be told? God, the giver of peace, is pervading all. Nanak begs for one gift: in your grace, give me the Naam. ॥4॥
1181.3: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As plants turn green on meeting water, so in the Saadh Sangat Haumai is shed. As a servant has confidence in his master, so the Guru, the Pir, is (our) support, the one who saves. You are the Giver, O God, the one who gives (to all); every moment I bow to him. He who obtains the Saadh Sangat, that person is dyed with the love of the Supreme Lord. They are freed from (their) bonds; the devotees worship (him), (and that is their) way of union. (The) eyes are content, beholding (his) sight; the tongue sings (his) countless virtues; thirst is quenched by the Guru's grace; the mind is sated with the taste of the Lord's delight. The servant is engaged in the service of the feet (of God), the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One. Your Name saves all; Nanak has found this treasure. ॥4॥
1181.4: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You are the great Giver, ever giving; you are pervading (all) souls and breaths of life. You have given all foods to eat; (yet) I, without virtue, do not acknowledge a single kindness (of yours). I know nothing of your worth; O merciful God, raise me up to the high state yourself. I have done no chanting, no austerities, no (ritual) deeds; I know no (right) way (of living) at all. In my mind I keep one hope: that by the support of your Name I will cross over. O God, you are skilled in all powers; (we are like) the fish in the water, who cannot find (its) end. Inaccessible, inaccessible, highest of the high are you; we are small, you are very great. Those who have meditated on you are rich; those who have found you are wealthy; whoever has served you is at peace: O Nanak, (they) have fallen at the refuge of the Sants. ॥4॥
1182.1: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Serve him who made you; worship him who gave (you) life. Become his servant, and then no penalty will fall on you; keep his treasury (as his potdar, his treasurer), and then no pain will touch you. The mortal who has such great fortune attains this state of Nirvana. In service to another, life is wasted; no purpose at all is fulfilled. The service of men is truly hard; the service of the Saadh is ever a comfort. If you long for lasting peace, O brother, the Guru has shown (the way): the Saadh Sangat. There one repeats only the Naam; the Saadh Sangat carries (one) across. Of all essences, the essence is (divine) wisdom; of all meditations, (the true) meditation is on the One; in the Kirtan of the Lord is the most sublime melody: O Nanak, meeting the Guru, sing (his) praises. ॥4॥
1182.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He uttering whom the mouth becomes pure, remembering whom one's repute is spotless, worshipping whom Jam says nothing (to one), by whose service one obtains everything: utter Ram, Ram; (utter) Ram, Ram; give up all the desires of the mind. He by whom earth and sky are upheld, whose light is in every heart, remembering whom the fallen becomes pure, and at the last moment does not weep again and again: (His Name) is the highest dharma among all dharmas, the deed above all rites and deeds; he whom godlike men and gods long for: (to find him,) join in the service of the assembly of the Sants. He to whom the Primal Being has given the gift has found the Lord, the treasure; his state and extent cannot be told: O servant Nanak, meditate on the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1182.3: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). A thirst took hold within (my) mind and body; the merciful Guru fulfilled my hope. In the Saadh Sangat (my) sins were cut away; I repeated the Naam, in love of the Lord's Name. By the Guru's grace spring has come into being: I have enshrined (his) lotus feet in my heart; for ever and ever I hear the Lord's praise. O all-powerful Master, doer and cause of all, I, without a master, am in your refuge, O God. All beings and creatures (live) by your support; in your grace, O God, carry (them) across. The Divine One, who ends the round of birth and destroys pain, is served by godlike men and silent sages; he in whose power earth and sky (rest): all creatures eat what you give. O merciful God, who knows the inner heart, look upon your servant with your glance of grace. In your grace, give me this gift, that Nanak may live, repeating your Name. ॥4॥
1183.1: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the love of Ram all sins are gone; repeating (the Name of) Ram, there is no anguish at all; repeating (the Name of) Gobind, all darkness is dispelled; remembering the Lord, there is no round (of births) at all. In my (home), spring is the love of Ram, (and) the company of the Sants for ever. The Sants have given (this) teaching: blessed is the land where a devotee of Gobind (dwells); a place without devotion to the Lord is a wilderness. By the Guru's grace, recognise (him) in every heart. (Take) the Kirtan of the Lord (as your) delights, pleasures and joy; O mind, always shrink from doing wrong. See God the Creator near (you): here and hereafter, God sets (your) affairs right. (My) attention is fixed on (his) lotus feet: in his grace God has given (this) gift. I long for the dust (of the feet) of your Sants; O Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Master, who is ever present. ॥4॥
1183.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The True Supreme God is ever new; by the Guru's grace I utter (his Name) day after day. God is (my) guardian, (my) mother and father, he by whose remembrance there is no anguish. I meditate on the Master with one mind, in one love; (I am) ever in the shelter of the perfect Guru; the True Master has kept (me), holding (me) to his bosom. God himself has protected his servants; all the wicked foes have wandered and grown weary. Without the True Guru there is no place (of refuge); (those who) keep running through lands and foreign lands (find only) pain. Their doings (and their record) will not be erased; they themselves eat what they have sown. He himself is the protector of his servant; no one can reach the servant (to harm him). God himself, making the effort, has protected (his) servants, he whose glory is unbroken and perfect. Ever sing with (your) tongue the praises of Gobind; Nanak lives, meditating on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
1183.3: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Serving the Guru's feet, pain has gone; the Supreme Lord God has shown mercy; all (my) longings and tasks are fulfilled: Nanak lives by repeating the Name of Ram. Lovely is that season in which the Lord comes to mind; without the True Guru (the world) appears to wail; the Saakat comes and goes again and again. They are wealthy who have the Lord God as (their) capital; through the Guru's Shabad (their) lust and anger are destroyed. (His) fears are gone, (he) has attained the state of fearlessness: meeting the Guru, Nanak has meditated on the Master. God has given (him) a dwelling in the Saadh Sangat; repeating, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, (his) hope is fulfilled. (The Lord) pervades the water, the land and the sky; meeting the Guru, Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. This (Name) is the eight siddhis and the nine treasures; it is obtained by grace, (by him) to whom (God) gives the Naam. O God, your servants live by repeating, repeating (your Name); O Nanak, meeting the Guru, (their heart-)lotus blossoms. ॥4॥
The eight siddhis: the miraculous powers of yoga (anima, laghima and the rest).
1184.1: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Iktuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Repeating (the Name), all desires are fulfilled; God has united (with himself) those long separated. Dwell on Gobind, who is worthy to be dwelt upon, dwelling on whom (one) enjoys the peace of Sahaj. In his grace (God) has looked (on him) with his glance of grace; he himself has taken care of his servant. The bed (of the heart) has become beautiful with (his) delight: God, the Master of peace, has come and met (me). He has not weighed my merits and faults; God has made Nanak a worshipper of (his) feet. ॥4॥
1184.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Singing (God's) praises, sins are destroyed; night and day the melody of Sahaj has sprung up (within). The mind has blossomed, (joined) with the Lord's feet: in (his) grace (he) has brought me to meet the holy; ever I am dyed in the love of the Lord's Name. In his grace Gopal has become manifest; attaching (me) to the hem of his robe, the Merciful to the meek has saved (me). This mind has turned into the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh; it ever sees the Master present. Lust, anger and craving are gone: O Nanak, God's grace has come (upon me). ॥4॥
1184.3: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). God himself has wiped out the diseases; placing his hands (on them), he has protected his children. In (my) home are peace and Sahaj; (there is) the spring that lasts for ever, (for we) have come to the refuge of the perfect Guru, (and) repeated the Mantra of the Lord, Har Har, the embodiment of well-being. God himself has cut away sorrow and anguish; meditate on your own Guru, day after day. The servant who repeats your Name obtains all fruits, singing (your) eternal virtues. O Nanak, good is the way of the devotees: they repeat (the Name of) the Giver of peace, day after day. ॥4॥
1184.4: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Issuing his Hukam, (he) has made (them) blissful; he has become merciful to his servant. The perfect Guru has made everything perfect; he has placed the Amrit Name in (my) heart. He did not weigh my deeds or my dharma at all; taking (me) by the arm, he carried (me) across the terrifying world-ocean. God has cut away the filth and made pure (those who) have fallen at the refuge of the perfect Guru. You yourself do (all), you yourself are the Doer; in (your) grace you have saved Nanak. ॥4॥
1185.1: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. See: flower upon flower has blossomed! Give up, give up (your) ego; cling to the lotus feet; meet God, O fortunate one. O my mind, remember the Lord. (Some trees grow) dense, fragrant and tender; some stay dried up, (hard) as wood. The season of spring has come: (only the one who remembers the Lord) stays in full bloom. Now Kalyug has come, O (brother): sow the One Name, sow (it); there is no other season (for it), none at all. Do not stray in doubt, do not stray. Meeting the Guru, he finds the Lord on whose forehead it is so written. O mind, (this) is the season of the Name; Nanak utters the praises of the Lord, Har Hare, Har Hare. ॥2॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
1185.2: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Gather together and meet, my brothers; fixing (your) attention (on the Lord), put away double-mindedness. Become partners in (the game of) the Lord's Name; spreading the cloth (of the board) through the Guru, sit down (to play). Cast the dice in this way, O brother: through the Guru, repeat the Naam day and night, (and) at the last moment no pain will strike (you). Make good deeds your chaupar board, and make truthful living your pieces; conquer lust, anger, greed and attachment: such a game is dear to the Lord. Rise at dawn and bathe (in the Name); even in sleep, worship the Lord. My True Guru carries (us) through the hard moves; in peace and Sahaj (we) go home. The Lord himself plays, himself watches; the Lord himself has made the creation. O servant Nanak, the man who plays through the Guru wins the game and comes home. ॥4॥
In the game of chaupar the pieces move round the board to reach home.
1185.3: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You alone know your creative power; no other knows (it). He on whom you show grace, O my Beloved, he alone recognises you. I am a sacrifice to your devotees; ever beautiful is your place, O God; your wonders are without end. Your service is done (only) by your (doing); no other can do it. He alone is your devotee who pleases you, he on whom you place (your) love. You are the great Giver, you are the great Wise One; there is no other. You are my all-powerful Master; what do I know of your worship? Your palace is beyond the reach of the senses, O my Beloved; hard is your Will (to walk in). Says Nanak, I have fallen down at your door: save me, foolish and ignorant (as I am). ॥4॥
1186.1: Raag Basant Hindol, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The world) does not understand (its) Root, does not know itself; it is caught in doubt, through ego. O Father, Supreme Lord, God, Master, carry me, who am without virtue, across. Creation and dissolution come from God: this is what the Lord's servants have reflected upon. Those who are dyed in the love of God's Name: I count them happy in Kalyug. No other means comes to mind; O Nanak, one crosses over by the Guru's word. ॥4॥
1186.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Basant Hindol, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, know this body to be false; Ram, who dwells within it: recognise him (alone) as true. This world is (like) wealth in a dream; why do you swell with pride, seeing it? Nothing (of it) goes with you; why do you cling to it? Give up both praise and slander (of others); bring the Lord's praise into (your) heart. O servant Nanak, the One Being, the Lord God, pervades all. ॥2॥
1186.3: Raag Basant, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Sinful lust dwells in the heart; so the fickle mind cannot be held in check. Yogis, jangams and sannyasis: on all of them this noose has been cast. Whoever has cherished the Lord's Name, they have crossed over the world-ocean. Servant Nanak (has come) to the Lord's refuge: give (him) the Naam, that he may go on singing (your) praises. ॥3॥
1186.4: Raag Basant, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mother, I have found the wealth of the Lord's Name; my mind is freed from running about, and has settled down to rest. Attachment to Maya has fled from (my) body; spotless wisdom has sprung up (within). Greed and attachment cannot touch (me): I have taken hold of devotion to the Lord God. The doubt of birth after birth has ended, since I found the jewel of the Name; all craving has perished from (my) mind; I am absorbed in the peace of (my) own self. He to whom the Treasure of mercy becomes kind sings the praises of Gobind; says Nanak, wealth of this kind some rare one obtains through the Guru. ॥3॥
1186.5: Raag Basant, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, why have you forgotten the Name of Ram? (When) the body perishes, (you) will have to deal with Jam. This world is a mountain of smoke; by what reasoning have you taken it to be real? Wealth, wife, property and house: nothing (of these) goes with (you); understand this. Devotion to Narayan alone goes with (you); says Nanak, meditate on him in single-minded love. ॥3॥
1187.1: Raag Basant, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Why have you strayed, O (man), attached to false greed? Nothing is lost yet: wake up even now. Know this world to be like a dream; it perishes in an instant: take this as true. The Lord ever dwells with you; night and day, O friend, meditate on him. At the final moment he will be (your) help; says Nanak, sing his praises. ॥3॥
1187.2: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis Dutuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The world (the soul caught in Maya) is a crow; the Name is not in its mind. See: forgetting the Name, it swoops down on the bait. Its mind keeps wavering, with ill intent in its heart. This false love for the world snaps (in the end). Lust and anger are poison, a load as crushing as a thunderbolt. Without the Name, how can there be a life of virtue? (This body is) a house of sand built in a whirlpool, see, a bubble raised as the rain comes down; (the Creator) turns his wheel and shapes it from a mere drop. The light in every being is the handmaid of the Name alone. O God, having brought all into being, you are the Guru, the crown over all. May I worship you and fall at your feet; steeped in the Name, I long for your shelter alone. Whoever goes on his way keeping the Name hidden is a thief. One who ties poison into the hem of his garment loses his honour; one steeped in the True Name goes home with honour. Whatever God does, he does by his own will; one who holds to his fear becomes fearless, O my mother. The lovely woman craves pleasure; (but) betel, flowers and sweet tastes are (all) diseases. The more she plays and delights, the more sorrow (she reaps). Coming into God's refuge, (she knows that) what he does is what comes to be. She puts on clothes and adorns herself much; her body of clay swells with pride, and her beauty turns to vice; hopes and desires have shut the door (to God); without the Name, house and home (the heart) lie desolate. Go forth, O daughter, O princess (my soul); make the most of the dawn and speak the Name of the True One; serve the Beloved, with God's love as your support; through the Guru's Shabad, put away the poisonous thirst (for Maya). Mohan, the Enchanter, has enchanted my mind; through the Guru's Shabad I have come to know you. O Nanak, (his servants) stand at God's door, longing (for him): in your Name (alone) they find contentment; be gracious. ॥8॥
1187.3: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The strayed mind wanders, coming and going; greedy beyond measure, it is lured by Maya, from which escape is hard. It is never seen steady, nor (held) in love of the One; like a fish, it gets the hook caught in its throat. The strayed mind comes to see (its error) through the True Name, when it reflects on the Guru's Shabad, naturally, in Sahaj. The strayed mind roams about like a bumblebee; through the senses it craves a host of empty vices. It is trapped like an elephant in the grip of lust, bound tight in chains and beaten on the head. The foolish mind is a frog, without devotion; empty of the Name, it is fallen from (God's) door and accursed. It has neither caste nor lineage, and none speaks its name; empty of virtues, its companions are sorrows alone. The mind is restless: hold it back, so that it does not wander off. Without being steeped in the Lord's essence, there is neither honour nor trust. (O God,) you yourself are the one who hears (all), you yourself the protector; having made the earth, he himself watches over it and knows (its needs). (When) he himself leads astray, to whom should I go and tell (it)? He brings (me) to the Guru; (to him) I tell my pain, O mother. Earning virtues, I give up my faults; one steeped in the Guru's Shabad merges in the True One. Meeting the True Guru, the understanding is raised high, the mind becomes pure, and one washes Haumai away. Such a one is ever free; no one can bind him; he ever speaks the Name, and nothing else. The mind comes and goes within the Lord's will; the One is in all, and nothing can be said (against him). The Hukam alone prevails in all, and all merge in the Hukam; pain and pleasure are all in his will. (O God,) you do not err; you never go astray; one to whom (the Guru) makes his Shabad heard gains an understanding beyond fathoming. You are the great Master, (dwelling) in the Shabad; praising the True One, Nanak's mind is won over. ॥8॥
1188.1: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The one who thirsts for the sight (of God) gives up duality and is absorbed in the One alone. His pain goes far away; churning (the Name), he eats Amrit; through the Guru he understands and merges in the One. So many cry out for the sight of you (O God), but only a rare one, joined to the Guru's Shabad, knows (you). The Vedas expound and say that one should speak of the One alone. He is without end: who has found his end? The One alone is the Creator who made the world and holds up the earth and the sky without any prop. Knowledge of the One, meditation on him and absorption in his praise (alone are true); the One alone needs no support, and his story cannot be told. The Shabad of the One alone is the true mark (of approval); the wise come to know this from the perfect Guru. Whoever makes the True One firm within as the one Dharam, he, through the Guru's teaching, is perfect in every age. With his mind held in one unbroken strain, he is steeped in the Limitless One; he, through the Guru, attains the unseen, boundless Lord. There is one throne and one King; (he is) in all places, and free of all care. The three worlds are his making; (he is their) essence; he is beyond reach, beyond the senses, the One Creator, Ekankar. His form is one, his Name everlasting; there (in his presence) true justice is done. One whose deeds are true is honoured and approved; he receives respect in the True Court. Devotion is to the One alone, and love for the One alone; without fear (of God) and devotion, there is coming and going. One who learns from the Guru and lives (in the world) as a guest, that servant, steeped in the Lord's essence, is approved. Here and hereafter I see (you), and in Sahaj I dwell on (you); I long for none but you, O Master. O Nanak, (to one who) has burnt away Haumai through the Shabad the True Guru has shown the true sight (of God). ॥8॥
1189.1: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The restless mind finds no far shore (to its restlessness); it comes and goes without a moment's delay. The suffering is great, O Creator; one dies of it; none but the Beloved takes care (of me). All are good: whom should I call low? Through devotion to the Lord, (my mind) is won over in the True Name. I have tried remedies beyond count and am worn out; how can the pain end without my Guru? Without devotion to the Lord there is pain upon pain, O my Master, giver of pain and pleasure. The disease is grave: how can I take heart? The one who understands the disease, he takes away the pain. There are faults in my mind and body; searching and seeking, the Guru has united (me with God), O brother. The Guru's Shabad, the Lord's Name, is the medicine; (O God,) as you keep me, so I live. The world itself is sick: whom should I seek out to show (my illness) to? The Lord is pure, and pure is his Name. The one who sees (God's) home within the home (of the heart) and shows it (to others), he, the Guru of the high mansion, calls (the soul) into the Mansion. (Their) mind stays within the mind, the consciousness within the consciousness; thus the Lord's people stay detached. They remain untouched by joy and grief; tasting Amrit, they dwell in the Lord's Name. One who knows his own self and keeps his mind attuned (to God) wins (the game of) life; through the Guru's teaching, his pain has fled. The Guru has given (me) the true Amrit, and I drink it; in Sahaj I die (to the vices), and while yet alive I truly live. (O God,) if it pleases the Guru, make (me) your own and keep (me); one who becomes yours merges in you alone. The pleasure-seeker is gripped by the pain of disease; (one to whom) God is seen pervading every heart is, through the Guru's Shabad, detached from pleasure and pain alike; O Nanak, he dwells on the Lord with love in his heart. ॥8॥
1189.2: Raag Basant, Iktuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O blind one, do not grow proud of (smearing yourself with) ashes: by these ways, by going naked, there is no Yoga (no union with God). O fool, why have you forgotten the Name of the Lord? (It alone) is of use to you at the last. Ask the Guru, and reflect: wherever I look, there is Saringpani (God). What can I say (of myself), when nothing is (mine)? (O God,) caste and honour, all lie in your Name. Why are you proud, looking at your goods and wealth? At the time of departing, nothing will be yours. Slay the five enemies and keep the mind in its place: this is the foundation of the way of Yoga. Haumai is a hobble on your mind; O fool, you do not remember the Lord, (through whom) you would go free. Forgetting the Lord, beware lest you fall into Jam's power, and, O fool, take blows at the last. If you reflect on the Guru's Shabad, self-conceit goes, and true Yoga comes to dwell in the mind. You do not remember the One who gave you soul and body; O fool, (dwelling at) tombs and cremation grounds is not Yoga. Nanak speaks the fine Word of (God's) virtues: open your eyes and recognise (it). ॥10॥
Saringpani: he who holds the bow Saarang, a name of Vishnu; here, God.
1190.1: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Deeds done in double-mindedness and evil understanding are blind; the manmukh wanders in pitch darkness. The blind mind follows a blind understanding; without the deeds the Guru teaches, doubt does not flee. The blind manmukhs have no liking for the Guru's teaching; they have become beasts, and their pride does not leave them. (God) has created the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life; as it pleases my Master, he creates them and draws them back into himself. All the world strays, with neither the Shabad nor right conduct; he alone understands whose guide is the Guru, the Creator. Those who serve the Guru are pleasing to the Master; he has forgiven them, and they are beholden to no Jam. Those in whose hearts the One alone is dear, he himself has united (them with himself), and he has ended their doubt. (God) depends on none, is without end and beyond all limit; the Creator is won over by truth. O Nanak, the Guru instructs those who stray; he shows (them) the One and keeps (them) steady in the True One. ॥8॥
1190.2: Raag Basant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). He himself is the bumblebee, the flower and the vine; he himself is the Sangat, bringing friends together in union. O bumblebee (my mind), take in such a fragrance that the trees break into flower and the forests turn green. He himself is Kavla (Lakshmi), and he himself her Husband; he himself establishes (the world) by his Word, and enjoys it. He himself is the calf, the cow and her milk; he is the house himself, its pillar and the body. He himself is the deed, and the doer; he himself, through the Guru, reflects. O Maker, you create and create, and watch over (all), giving the support of your light to countless beings. You are the lake and the ocean, the deep (ocean) of virtues; you are without lineage, untouched by Maya, the supreme diamond. You yourself are the Creator, able to do all; O King, you are free of all desire, and your people are at peace. O Nanak, (they) are filled with the taste of the Lord's Name; without the Lord, the Beloved Guru, life is in vain. ॥8॥
1190.3: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O God,) making nine (regions), seven (continents), fourteen (worlds), three (realms) and four (ages), you peopled the mansion (of the world) through the four (sources of life); the four lamps (the Vedas) you placed in the hands of the four (ages), each in its turn. O Merciful One, O Madhusudan, O Madho, such is your power. In every house (body) is your fire, (all beings are) your army, and Dharam (Raj) rules (over them) as chief; the earth is your cauldron, from which (each) receives (his share) once (as it is written); destiny is your storekeeper. (Yet man) is not content and begs again and again; Narad (the fickle mind) brings (him) to ruin. Greed is a dark prison, and faults are iron fetters on the feet. (His) capital (is that) he is beaten daily with clubs, and sin sits over (him) as the kotwal. Good or bad, (one becomes) as your glance falls. The Primal Being is now called Allah; the turn of the sheikhs has come; the temples of the gods are taxed; such is the custom that has spread. (Now) the ewer, the call to prayer, the namaz and the prayer mat (prevail), and blue is the garb, O Banwari; in every home all beings say Mian; the speech of your (people) has become another. If you, the King, the Lord of the earth, the Master, (will it so), what power have we? (The people of) the four corners will bow in salaam (to you), and in every home will be your praise. From pilgrimages, the Simritis, merit and charity comes a little profit, a day's wage; O Nanak, glory is gained by cherishing the Name for even a moment. ॥8॥
1191.1: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. In the town of the body lives a child (the mind) that does not stay still for an instant. (People) have worn themselves out with countless means and efforts; again and again it wanders. O my Master, bring the child home to one place. When the True Guru is met, the Perfect One is found: meditate on the Name of the Lord, the mark (of approval). This body is a corpse, a heap of clay, and so is the whole world, wherever the Lord's Name has not come to dwell. The Guru let fall the water of the Lord's Name, and it turned green again, full of sap. Looking and looking, I searched the whole body, and through the Guru one wondrous play was shown (to me): all the Saakats died searching outside; through the Guru's teaching, I found the Lord within the home (of the heart). (God) has been merciful to the poorest of the poor, as Krishna came to Bidar's house. Sudama came to meet (him) in faith, and before (he went home) his poverty was ended and everything was there. Great is the honour of the Lord's Name; my Master himself has kept it. Even if all the Saakats speak ill, he has not let it lessen by a grain or a sesame seed. The Lord's Name is the glory of his servant; he has won renown in all ten directions. The slandering Saakat cannot bear it in the least; he has set a firebrand to his own house. Meeting the Lord's servant, his servant is honoured; virtue shines forth in virtue. Those servants of my Master are dear to the Beloved who become the slaves of (his) slaves. The infinite Creator is himself the water; it is he who unites (us) in union. O Nanak, through the Guru he unites (them) in Sahaj, as water merges in water. ॥8॥
Bidar (Vidura): born of a maidservant, a devotee of Krishna.
1192.1: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, Dutuki, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, hear the story (of the devotees) and repeat (the Name) with love: Ajamal was saved by uttering (the Name) once; Balmik found the Saadh Sangat; Dhru met the Lord face to face. (O God,) I ask for the dust of your Sants' feet; be gracious and give (it), that I may take it and put it on my forehead. Ganika was saved as the parrot spoke the Lord's (Name); Gajindra meditated (on the Lord), and the Lord set him free; (he) ended the poverty of Sudama the Brahmin; O mind, you too meditate on Gobind. (He) saved the hunter who struck (Krishna) with an arrow; Kubija was saved by the touch of (his) thumb; (he) saved Bidar for (his) spirit of service; O mind, you too meditate on the Lord. The Lord himself kept Prahlad's honour; as her clothes were being stripped, (he) kept Dropati's honour; whoever served (him) at the very last (was saved); O mind, serve (him), and you will cross over. Dhanna served (God) with a child's innocent mind; meeting the Guru, Trilochan attained perfection; the Guru gave Beni (inner) light; O mind, you too become (his) servant. Jaidev gave up his ego; Sain the barber was saved by service; (their) mind does not falter or waver or go off anywhere; O mind, you too will cross over by taking (his) refuge. Those on whom the Master himself has shown favour, those devotees (O God) you have saved; you weighed none of their merits or faults; seeing this way of yours, (my) mind has taken to (your) service. Kabir meditated (on God) with single-minded love; the dear Lord dwells with Namdev; Ravidas meditated on God, the Incomparable; Guru Nanak Dev is the very form of Govind. ॥8॥
Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called on his son Narayan. Kubija: the hunchbacked maid of Kans, made straight and fair by Krishna.
1192.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through countless births (beings) wander from species to species; without remembering the Lord, they fall into hell. Without devotion, (the mind) is broken into pieces; without understanding, Jam deals out punishment. Meditate on Gobind for ever, my friend; love the True Shabad for ever. In no task does contentment come (to one drunk on Maya); all Maya's shows are clouds of smoke. He does not shrink from committing sins; drunk on (Maya's) poison, he comes and goes. Saying I, I, the vices grow; the world is drowned in attachment and greed. Lust and anger hold (his) mind in their power; not even in a dream has he taken the Lord's Name. Now a king, now a beggar, the world is bound in pain and pleasure. There is no effort (in him) to save the mind; the bonds of sin keep falling (on him) every day. Of loved ones and friends, none is a companion; (beings) sow and themselves eat (the harvest). The things for whose gathering vices are done, the fool leaves in an instant and departs. In attachment to Maya he has wandered much; by the lines of his past deeds he does deeds (again). The Maker himself is untouched; on God no virtue or sin leaves a stain. Save (me), O merciful Gobind; (I am in) your refuge, O perfect and gracious One. Apart from you there is no other place (for me); in your grace, O God, give (me) the Naam. You are the Creator, you are the Doer of all; you are high, you are utterly beyond limit. In your grace, attach (me) to the hem of your robe: servant Nanak (has come to) God's refuge. ॥8॥
1193.1: Basant ki Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Meditate on the Lord's Name, O brother, and turn green. This lovely season is gained by the grace written (in one's lot); the woods, the grass and the three worlds have blossomed, and found the fruit of Amrit. Meeting the Saadh, peace wells up, and all the soot (of the mind) is gone. Nanak remembers the one Name, and never again runs about (from birth to birth). (For one) who has made the true offering, (God) has bound the five enemies, mighty as they are; (God) has made (him) meditate on his own feet, and the Merciful One stands within (him). All (his) disease and sorrow are gone; he is ever fresh and whole. Day and night he meditates on the Name, and never again falls into death. O Nanak, he has become again the One from whom he sprang. Where does (a being) come from, where does it dwell, into what does it merge? All beings and creatures are the Master's: who can tell his worth? Those who ever speak of him, meditate on him and hear of him are devotees who look beautiful. The Master is beyond reach, beyond the senses; no other can equal him. The perfect Guru has taught the True One, and Nanak makes him heard. ॥3॥
1193.2: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The earth has blossomed, the sky has blossomed; in every heart the light of the Supreme Soul has blossomed. Ram the King has blossomed in ways without end; wherever I look, there he is, pervading all. Further, the four Vedas have blossomed (by his light); the Simritis have blossomed, and the Kateb with them. Shankar (Shiva) has blossomed in yogic meditation; Kabir's Master (blossoms) alike in all. ॥3॥
The Kateb: the scriptures of the Semitic faiths (the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran).
1193.3: The pandits are drunk on their reading of the Puranas; the yogis are drunk on their yoga and meditation; the sannyasis are drunk on their ego; the ascetics are drunk on the secrets of their austerities. All are drunk with the wine (of pride); none is awake; and the thieves who live alongside them are busy looting the house. Sukdev is awake, and Akrur; Hanuman is awake, though he bears a tail; Shankar is awake, serving (the Lord's) feet; in Kalyug, Nama and Jaidev are awake. Waking and sleeping are of many kinds; to wake through the Guru: that alone is the best. (The Name) is of great use to this embodied soul; says Kabir: meditate on the Name of Ram. ॥3॥
Sukdev, the son of the sage Vyas, recited the Bhagavat Purana to King Parikshit; Akrur was a devotee of Krishna; Hanuman is the servant of Ram.
1194.1: The wife has given birth to her husband; the son has set his father at play; without breasts, milk has been given to drink.
