Gajindra meditated (on the Lord), and the Lord set him free;
(he) ended the poverty of Sudama the Brahmin;
O mind, you too meditate on Gobind.
(He) saved the hunter who struck (Krishna) with an arrow;
Kubija was saved by the touch of (his) thumb;
(he) saved Bidar for (his) spirit of service;
O mind, you too meditate on the Lord.
The Lord himself kept Prahlad's honour;
as her clothes were being stripped, (he) kept Dropati's honour;
whoever served (him) at the very last (was saved);
O mind, serve (him), and you will cross over.
Dhanna served (God) with a child's innocent mind;
meeting the Guru, Trilochan attained perfection;
the Guru gave Beni (inner) light;
O mind, you too become (his) servant.
Jaidev gave up his ego;
Sain the barber was saved by service;
(their) mind does not falter or waver or go off anywhere;
O mind, you too will cross over by taking (his) refuge.
Those on whom the Master himself has shown favour,
those devotees (O God) you have saved;
you weighed none of their merits or faults;
seeing this way of yours, (my) mind has taken to (your) service.
Kabir meditated (on God) with single-minded love;
the dear Lord dwells with Namdev;
Ravidas meditated on God, the Incomparable;
Guru Nanak Dev is the very form of Govind. ॥8॥
1192.2: Raag Basant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through countless births (beings) wander from species to species;
without remembering the Lord, they fall into hell.
Without devotion, (the mind) is broken into pieces;
without understanding, Jam deals out punishment.
Meditate on Gobind for ever, my friend;
love the True Shabad for ever.
In no task does contentment come (to one drunk on Maya);
all Maya's shows are clouds of smoke.
He does not shrink from committing sins;
drunk on (Maya's) poison, he comes and goes.
Saying I, I, the vices grow;
the world is drowned in attachment and greed.
Lust and anger hold (his) mind in their power;
not even in a dream has he taken the Lord's Name.
Now a king, now a beggar,
the world is bound in pain and pleasure.
There is no effort (in him) to save the mind;
the bonds of sin keep falling (on him) every day.
Of loved ones and friends, none is a companion;
(beings) sow and themselves eat (the harvest).
The things for whose gathering vices are done,
the fool leaves in an instant and departs.
In attachment to Maya he has wandered much;
by the lines of his past deeds he does deeds (again).
The Maker himself is untouched;
on God no virtue or sin leaves a stain.
Save (me), O merciful Gobind;
(I am in) your refuge, O perfect and gracious One.
Apart from you there is no other place (for me);
in your grace, O God, give (me) the Naam.
You are the Creator, you are the Doer of all;
you are high, you are utterly beyond limit.
In your grace, attach (me) to the hem of your robe:
servant Nanak (has come to) God's refuge. ॥8॥
1193.1: Basant ki Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Meditate on the Lord's Name, O brother, and turn green.
This lovely season is gained by the grace written (in one's lot);
the woods, the grass and the three worlds have blossomed, and found the fruit of Amrit.
Meeting the Saadh, peace wells up, and all the soot (of the mind) is gone.
Nanak remembers the one Name, and never again runs about (from birth to birth).
(For one) who has made the true offering, (God) has bound the five enemies, mighty as they are;
(God) has made (him) meditate on his own feet, and the Merciful One stands within (him).
All (his) disease and sorrow are gone; he is ever fresh and whole.
Day and night he meditates on the Name, and never again falls into death.
O Nanak, he has become again the One from whom he sprang.
Where does (a being) come from, where does it dwell, into what does it merge?
All beings and creatures are the Master's: who can tell his worth?
Those who ever speak of him, meditate on him and hear of him are devotees who look beautiful.
The Master is beyond reach, beyond the senses; no other can equal him.
The perfect Guru has taught the True One, and Nanak makes him heard. ॥3॥
1193.2: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The earth has blossomed, the sky has blossomed;
in every heart the light of the Supreme Soul has blossomed.
Ram the King has blossomed in ways without end;
wherever I look, there he is, pervading all.
Further, the four Vedas have blossomed (by his light);
the Simritis have blossomed, and the Kateb with them.
Shankar (Shiva) has blossomed in yogic meditation;
1193.3: The pandits are drunk on their reading of the Puranas;
the yogis are drunk on their yoga and meditation;
the sannyasis are drunk on their ego;
the ascetics are drunk on the secrets of their austerities.
All are drunk with the wine (of pride); none is awake;
and the thieves who live alongside them are busy looting the house.
Hanuman is awake, though he bears a tail;
Shankar is awake, serving (the Lord's) feet;
in Kalyug, Nama and Jaidev are awake.
Waking and sleeping are of many kinds;
to wake through the Guru: that alone is the best.
(The Name) is of great use to this embodied soul;
says Kabir: meditate on the Name of Ram. ॥3॥
1194.1: The wife has given birth to her husband;
the son has set his father at play;
without breasts, milk has been given to drink.
Look, people, at the sway of Kalyug:
the son has brought his own mother home as his bride.
without a mouth, he laughs and laughs;
without sleep, the man lies down and sleeps;
without a vessel, he churns milk.
Without udders, the cow is in milk;
with no journey to make, the road is long.
Without the True Guru the way is not found:
1194.2: Prahlad was sent to school;
he took many boys along as companions.
(He said to the teacher:) Why do you teach me the tangles of household affairs?
On my slate write: Sri Gopal.
I will not give up the Name of Ram, O Baba;
I have nothing to do with any other learning.
Sanda and Marka went and told (the king);
(the king) hastily sent for Prahlad.
(The teacher said:) Give up your habit of saying Ram;
I will have you freed at once; do as I say.
(Prahlad answered:) Why do you torment me again and again?
God has made the waters, the land, the hills and the mountains;
I will not forsake the One Ram; (that would) bring reproach on my guru.
Throw me (into the fire) and burn me, or kill me, as you will.
(Harnakhash) drew his sword and blazed with anger:
Tell me who your protector is.
God came forth from the pillar, taking on a vast form,
and slew Harnakhash, tearing him open with his nails.
He is the Supreme Being, the God above the gods,
who for the sake of devotion took the form of Narasimha.
Says Kabir: no one can perceive his limit;
(he) saved Prahlad many times. ॥5॥
1194.3: Within this body and mind (dwells) Madan (Kamdev, lust), a thief,
who has stolen my jewel of wisdom.
I am helpless, O God; to whom shall I tell (it)?
Who has not been brought to ruin (by him)? And who am I?
O Madho, this terrible pain cannot be borne;
what power have I against my fickle understanding?
Sanak, Sanandan, Shiva, Suk and the rest,
Brahma and the others born of the lotus of the navel,
the poets, the yogis and those with matted hair:
all of them got through their time as best they could, and departed.
You are fathomless; I cannot fathom you;
O God, Master of the meek, to whom (but you) shall I tell my pain?
Soothe my pain of birth and death, (born) of Maya,
O Ocean of peace, that I, Kabir, may dwell on your virtues. ॥3॥
1194.4: There is one master (of the caravan), and five traders;
there are twenty-five oxen, (but) the company is unsound;
there are nine carrying-poles and ten sacks,
and seventy-two ropes are bound about them.
I have no business with such a trade,
in which the capital dwindles and the interest grows day by day.
Together (the five) have traded in seven kinds of yarn,
and taken along the leanings of past deeds;
the three toll-collectors pick a quarrel;
The capital is lost, the trade is broken off;
the caravan has broken up and gone off to the ten directions.
Says Kabir: O mind, (your) work will be done;
once (you) merge in Sahaj, doubt flees. ॥3॥
1195.1: Raag Basant Hindol, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The mother is impure, and the father impure too; the fruits (the children) they bear are impure;
impure they come, impure they go, and impure the unfortunate die.
Tell me, O pandit, which place is pure,
where I may sit and eat my food?
The tongue is impure, (its) speech impure; ears and eyes are all impure;
O you scorched in the fire of Brahmin pride, the impurity of the organ of lust never washes off.
The fire too is impure, the water impure, and impure she who sat and cooked;
impure the ladle with which (he) began to serve, and impure the one who sat and ate.
The cow-dung is impure, the kitchen square impure, and impure the line drawn (round it).
Says Kabir: they alone are pure in whom true understanding has dawned. ॥4॥
1195.2: Raag Basant, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Ramanand Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Where should one go, O brother? Delight has come to (my own) home;
my thoughts do not wander; my mind has become lame (and goes nowhere).
One day a longing arose in my mind;
grinding sandalwood, (taking) perfume and many sweet scents,
I set out to worship at the place of God (the temple);
(but) the Guru showed me that God within my own mind.
Wherever one goes, there is (only) water and stone;
(O Lord,) you are filling all alike.
I have searched through all the Vedas and Puranas;
one should go there only if he is not here.
O True Guru, I am a sacrifice to you,
who have cut away all my bewildering doubts.
the Guru's Shabad cuts away (the bonds of) millions of deeds. ॥3॥
1195.3: Raag Basant, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
If the master puts (his servant) in hardship and the servant runs away,
(that servant) does not live long, and brings shame on both his families.
I will not give up devotion to you, even if the world laughs;
(your) lotus feet dwell in my heart.
As a man is ready to die for his wealth,
so the Sants do not give up the Name of Ram.
(Pilgrimage to) the Ganga, Gaya and the Godavari is a worldly business;
only if Narayan is well pleased is Nama (truly his) servant. ॥3॥
1196.1: The wave of greed roars mightily like a mountain torrent; my body is sinking, O Keshav.
Carry (me) across the world-ocean, O Gobind; carry me across, O Father Bithal.
I cannot steer the boat in the gale; I have not found your far shore, O Bithal.
Be merciful, and unite me with the True Guru, who may carry (me) across, O Keshav.
Says Nama: I cannot even swim; hold out your arm to me, hold out your arm, O Bithal. ॥4॥
1196.2: At first the cart, laden with dirt (soiled clothes), moves slowly;
behind, (the washerwoman) drives it on with a twig in her hand.
As she drives it towards the watering place, calling thru-titi,
(so) the darling (soul-bride) has set out to wash at the pool.
The washerman, dyed in love, does the washing;
my mind is dyed in the Lord's feet.
and has shown mercy to his devotee. ॥3॥
1196.3: Raag Basant, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O body,) you see nothing at all;
seeing your finery, you puff up with pride.
There is no place for the proud one;
the crow (of death) caws over your neck.
Why are you proud, you foolish one?
You are like the great mushroom of Bhadon (the rainy month), and quicker even than it to pass away.
As the deer has not found the secret:
the fragrance (of musk) is in its own body, (yet) it searches far afield (for it).
Whoever reflects on his own body,
him Jam's servant does not torment.
You pride yourself on son and wife;
(but) the Master will call (you) to account;
the soul suffers the pain of its own misdeeds;
afterwards, whom will you call, crying beloved, beloved?
If you take the shelter of the Saadh,
all your sins, millions upon millions, will be wiped away.
Says Ravidas: one who repeats the Naam
has nothing more to do with caste, with birth or with the forms of life. ॥4॥
1196.4: Raag Basant, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O dog,) your gait is like a cow's;
the hair on your tail gleams.
Seek out and eat whatever is in this house (of your own);
do not go to anyone else's (house) at all.
You lick the grinding-stone and eat the flour;
where will you carry off the grinding-stone's rag?
Your eyes are fixed hard on the hanging basket;
beware lest a stick or a club come down on your back.
Says Kabir: you have had your fill of pleasures;
beware lest someone strike you with a brick or a clod. ॥4॥
